title: Saying things
summary: Print a line, then print one built out of a variable.
explanation: say prints whatever follows it. Text in double quotes is printed as written. A name in single quotes is looked up first, so 'who' below prints Ada, not the word who.
code:
note: line one of every E++ program
Define who as "Ada".
say "Hello, world!"
say "Hello, " plus 'who' plus "."

title: Names and values
summary: Store a value, change it, do arithmetic on it.
explanation: Define gives a name to a starting value. Set replaces it later. Increase and decrease add and take away. Numbers do not need quotes; words do.
code:
Define score as 10.
Increase score by 5.
Decrease score by 2.
say "Score: " plus 'score'
Set score to 'score' times 2
say "Doubled: " plus 'score'

title: Asking questions
summary: Read an answer from the person using the program.
explanation: ask prints a question and waits. The answer is stored under the name you give and can be used like any other value. In the IDE the answer comes from the Answers box, so a program can be run the same way twice.
code:
ask "What is your name?" and save answer as name
say "Nice to meet you, " plus 'name' plus "."
ask "How old are you?" and save answer as age
if 'age' is greater than 12 then
  say "That is old enough for the next lesson."
otherwise
  say "Still plenty of time."
end if

title: Making decisions
summary: Compare values and pick a path through the program.
explanation: An if line reads as a sentence: 'x' is greater than 5. Otherwise handles everything else, and otherwise if adds another test. End if closes the block. Indentation is only for people; E++ uses the end line.
code:
Define temperature as 31.

if 'temperature' is greater than 30 then
  say "It is a hot one."
otherwise if 'temperature' is greater than 20 then
  say "Pleasant."
otherwise
  say "Bring a jacket."
end if

title: Doing it again
summary: Counted loops, conditional loops, and how to leave them.
explanation: repeat ... times runs a block a fixed number of times; the block ends at end repeat. while ... do keeps going while the test holds true. loopback ends the round it is in early and starts the next one, which is handy when the rest of the round no longer matters.
code:
repeat 3 times
  say "Round"
end repeat

define left as 4
while 'left' is greater than 0 do
  say "Left: " plus 'left'
  decrease left by 1
end while

define step as 0
repeat 5 times
  increase step by 1
  if 'step' is exactly equal to 3 then
    say "Round three skips the rest of itself."
    loopback
  end if
  say "Round " plus 'step'
end repeat

title: Libraries
summary: Math, Text, Random, Image, Draw and Python, one line at a time.
explanation: A library is a set of extra words. The line add library "Math" turns on the Math words for the rest of the file, and every library is switched on the same way. A file that loads libraries is saved with .eppla at the end; save this lesson that way and try it.
code:
add library "Math"
add library "Text"
add library "Random"

say square root of 225
display 7 divided by 8 as fraction
display 15 percent of 240
say uppercase of "quiet words"
say random number between 1 and 6

title: Sprites and pictures
summary: Move something around, and show an image of a real thing.
explanation: A sprite is a name with a position. Move right, left, up and down change that position by the number of pixels you write, and the dashboard draws the result so you can see it. Pictures work the other way round: a picture is Base64 text from a file, and display image sends it to the console.
code:
add library "Draw"
add library "Image"

define rover as drawing sprite
repeat 4 times
  'rover' move right "50 px"
  'rover' move down "20 px"
end repeat
say "Look at the dashboard to see where 'rover' went."

note: one green pixel, written as Base64
define dot as image "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mNk+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
check if "dot" exists
display image

title: Python, when you want it
summary: Drop into Python for a block, then come back to E++.
explanation: python code opens a block that runs as Python until end python, and print writes to the same console as say. What is inside the block is Python: indentation matters, and so do the brackets. The supported pieces are printing, if and elif, for, while, lists, and the usual number and text functions.
code:
add library "Python"

python code
  total = 0
  for number in range(1, 6):
      total += number
  print("Total:", total)
  for name in ["Ada", "Grace", "Alan"]:
      print(name, len(name))
end python

say "Back in E++."
